subject: Month-end vitals readout: latency, cost, uptime, usage — readout + owners
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Wong <emma.wong@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Month-end vitals readout: latency, cost, uptime, usage — readout + owners

Team —

Attaching the month-end vitals snapshot for May (pdf + raw cost CSV). Key callouts up front:

- Latency: p95 for text-generation climbed from 240ms -> 310ms week-over-week on hosted-1 due to a model rollout; p50 stayed ~120ms.
- Cost: unit token cost up ~13% driven by increased tail usage and fewer cache hits on long-chat sessions.
- Uptime: we had a 40-minute degraded period on 2027-05-24 UTC tied to a failing autoscaler config in Dedicated pools (timeline attached).
- Usage: daily active routes increased 18% month-over-month from two new customers (Acme Analytics is one).

Immediate asks:
1) Markus — please own a short (1 pager) hypothesis doc on the latency regression and a target remediation plan by EOD Fri (2027-05-28). Include whether we roll back rollout or patch runtime kernel selection.
2) Jonas — confirm root cause for the 5/24 degraded window and propose an SLA credit posture for impacted customers. I put the incident timeline draft in the attachments.
3) Marissa — consolidate potential top-3 cost levers (batching, quantization variant, KV cache policy) and expected unit cost delta; aim for a comms note for leadership by Mon 5/31.

Cc'd Emma at Acme — noted your uptick in queries; if any of your traffic experienced visible errors during 5/24 please flag here.

I'll run a 20-min readout for execs on Mon 5/31 at 3pm PT; please have updates in the shared Drive by then.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2027-05-monthly_vitals_dashboard.pdf (pdf), cost_drilldown_202705.csv (csv), uptime-incident-timeline-0524.docx (docx)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Wong <emma.wong@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Month-end vitals readout: latency, cost, uptime, usage — readout + owners

Thanks Laura — quick ack. I pulled the perf traces and model rollout logs. Two quick notes:

- The rollout we shipped on 5/18 included a new attention kernel that improves long-context throughput but has increased per-step overhead at short sequence lengths. The p95 regression tracks a distribution shift toward more short-turn dialog requests (lower average tokens per request).
- Rolling back the kernel will restore previous p95 but cost per token will rise ~6% (estimated); patching the kernel to bifurcate execution paths requires a couple-day engine change.

I'll draft the 1-pager and include a matrix: rollback vs patch vs traffic-split. Sending by Thu 5/27 COB.

-Markus

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Wong <emma.wong@acme-analytics.com>, Naresh Shah <naresh@zephyrcloud.io>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Month-end vitals readout: latency, cost, uptime, usage — readout + owners

Laura/Markus —

I confirmed the degraded window timeline and root cause: the Dedicated autoscaler incorrectly applied a scale-in policy during a transient spike in background health checks, which triggered a cascade when a single placement group lost capacity. Sequence: health checker spike -> scale-in -> placement fragment -> scheduler retries -> degraded responses (partial 503s) for 40m.

Impact: a subset of customers on dedicated pool "ded-nyc-2" saw elevated errors; we did not cross the 99.9% hit for tenant-level SLA in aggregate but it is borderline for a few customers (Acme included).

Attached: uptime-incident-timeline-0524.docx (with logs and trace IDs), proposed postmortem skeleton, and recommended immediate config change (disable aggressive scale-in under health-check spikes).

Proposed credit posture: for affected customers suggest a one-time partial credit equal to 3% of monthly committed usage for May (draft note in Drive). If leadership prefers conservative approach, escalate to finance.

-Jonas

> On Wed, 26 May 2027 10:11:00 -0700 Markus Klein wrote:
> > Thanks Laura — quick ack. I pulled the perf traces and model rollout logs.

Thanks for the heads up. We saw ~35 minutes of elevated error rates in our production run during 5/24 02:15–02:55 UTC. We recorded retries and some dropped payloads; we've attached our internal request IDs. Happy to share more data if useful for the postmortem.

One ask: can you confirm whether a credit will be applied automatically for affected committed customers or we should expect a manual adjustment? Our billing contact is cc'd on this thread.

—Emma
Product Lead, Analytics
Acme Analytics

Thanks all — status update before the 3pm PT exec readout: 

- Markus: 1-pager submitted to Drive (section: rollback vs patch). Short recommendation: traffic-split at edge + fast rollback threshold.
- Jonas: incident postmortem skeleton uploaded; recommended credit posture is 3% for impacted committed accounts.
- Marissa: cost lever summary in Drive — expected unit cost reduction if we apply KV cache TTL tweak + modest quantized variant rollout is ~9%.

Operational asks for the exec readout (3pm PT):
- Decision: accept proposed credit posture for Acme and any other impacted committed customers (Jonas to finalize list).
- Decision: approve traffic-split + rollback threshold to mitigate latency while we patch kernel (Markus will present tradeoffs).
- Commit: Marissa to run a quick internal experiment on KV policy next 48h and report observed cache-hit delta.

I'll present the dashboard top-lines; please be on the readout. Emma — thanks for the data; we'll include a note in the customer comms.

Laura

Attachments referenced: 2027-05-monthly_vitals_dashboard.pdf, cost_drilldown_202705.csv
